title: Nigeria through time
note: A pilot timeline of selected moments; this is not a complete history.

events.title: Independence
events.summary: Nigeria became independent from Britain as a federation with a parliamentary government. The moment followed decades of political organising and constitutional negotiation.

events.title: The Nigerian Civil War
events.summary: War followed the Eastern Region’s declaration of Biafra. Civilians endured mass displacement, hunger and violence. Its consequences continue to shape public memory and debates about the federation.

events.title: The war ends
events.summary: Biafra’s surrender ended the civil war. Reconstruction, relief and reconciliation became urgent tasks for communities across the affected regions.

events.title: Wole Soyinka receives the Nobel Prize
events.summary: The Nigerian playwright and poet received the Nobel Prize in Literature, a landmark in the international recognition of African writing.

events.title: Return to civilian rule
events.summary: Olusegun Obasanjo was sworn in as an elected president, beginning the Fourth Republic after a long period of military government. The 1999 constitution entered into force the same day.
events.sourceLabel: Federal Ministry of Information and WIPO Lex

events.title: Paris Club debt agreement
events.summary: Nigeria negotiated a major debt treatment with Paris Club creditors, combining debt relief with payments and buybacks. The deal substantially changed the country’s external debt position.
